findings.criterion: Bug 'Regression investigation: tickets branch/store exceeds 1 GiB after history reclaim' is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces and expected behavior holds.
findings.detail: The ticket explicitly states 'No production-code repair is authorized in this ticket' and 'No production files were changed and no repair/rewrite was attempted in this investigation.' The investigation confirmed the >1 GiB state still reproduces from a fresh clone at tip 2fd4a1a62c92f534825097153dd1767e97ec4b47 (checked-out tree 1,116,577,792 allocated bytes). The ticket is still in_progress and the remediation plan defers actual reclaim to follow-on tickets (irongray-unlucky-discus, epidemic-chocolaty-imago, etc.). The root cause was identified but the defect was not remediated — the store still exceeds 1 GiB.
findings.remediation: This is a read-only investigation ticket; the actual fix is delegated to irongray-unlucky-discus (targeted reclaim) and epidemic-chocolaty-imago (budgets). The bug criterion c05 can only be marked met after those follow-on tickets complete and a fresh clone confirms the store no longer exceeds 1 GiB. Record that outcome as a ticket comment with the post-reclaim clone tip, measured allocated bytes, and run/date.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
